sections.name: File setup, pct
sections.title: Chart size and helpers
sections.what: Sets the chart size and margin, adds a percent formatter, and imports the notebook type.
sections.why: Likely reason: one fixed size keeps all charts uniform.

sections.name: Frame
sections.title: Shared chart frame
sections.what: Wraps any chart in a figure with a screen reader label, a box, a drawing area and a collapsible data table.
sections.why: The file comment says each chart is an image with text and a table.
sections.watch_out: The label is the only description screen reader users get, so it must stay accurate.

sections.name: ReliabilityDiagram
sections.title: Calibration diagram
sections.what: Plots stated confidence against how often calls at that level were right, with a dashed perfect line. Larger dots mean more calls, and small samples are drawn hollow.
sections.why: The code comment says the diagonal line shows perfect calibration.
sections.watch_out: Buckets with no results are skipped in the drawing, but a missing hit rate is described as zero percent.

sections.name: LineOverCalls
sections.title: Line over calls
sections.what: Draws a line of values across call numbers, scaled to the data, with an option to keep a minimum span so small changes stay visible.
sections.why: The code comment says ratings sit far from zero, so the scale is set to the data.
sections.watch_out: A scale starting at zero can flatten small changes; the fromZero option turns that off.

sections.name: SkillRadar
sections.title: Skill radar
sections.what: Draws one spoke per skill area with the hit rate on each, places unplayed areas at the centre, and labels the edge.
sections.why: The code comment says unplayed areas sit at the centre.
sections.watch_out: Unplayed areas look like a 0 percent hit rate, which can mislead; the table shows the difference.

summary: Small hand-drawn charts for the Notebook: a calibration diagram, a line chart and a skill radar. Each has a text description and a data table.
purpose: Shows how well a fan's confidence matches results, how their scores move, and how they do in each skill area.
why: The file's opening comment says each chart is an image with a text description and a data table, for accessibility.
how: Each chart converts its data to positions on a shared drawing area and draws SVG shapes. A shared frame adds a label for screen readers, the drawing, and a collapsible data table.
inputs: Notebook data: calibration buckets, a list of points, and domain results.
outputs: Three SVG figures, each with a description and a table.
risks: Small samples are marked but still drawn. Spreading very long lists into min and max calls can fail on huge lists. A missing hit rate is drawn as zero.
debug: If a chart is empty, check the data passed in. If a point is off, check the scaling in that chart. If a table is missing, check the frame.
